notesStmt.note: Whitman contemplated writing an essay about Elias Hicks for many years. While finishing preparations for the printing of November Boughs, Whitman told Horace Traubel, "Some of these bits were written as many as thirty years ago. Some of them I have written within the past year. They are a miscellaneous lot but they all belong in the same stream" (see Traubel, With Walt Whitman in Camden, 2:42). It is therefore difficult to determine the exact date of the present manuscript, although the handwriting suggests a date in the 1880s. The leaf has been pasted to a backing sheet, rendering the verso inaccessible.

note.p: This short note refers to a passage in the third edition of Edward FitzGerald's Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám, the Astronomer-Poet of Persia, published in 1872. In his essay "Elias Hicks, Notes (such as they are)," Whitman quotes stanza 66 of FitzGerald's work. The current manuscript suggests that Whitman had considered including, in a footnote, the next three stanzas of the Rubáiyát, but the printed essay, which was first published in November Boughs (1888) lacks such a note.
